exposure: Active management protocol for suspected fetal macrosomia (EFW >=97th custom percentile at 34+0/35+6 weeks, 100-g OGTT, follow-up scan at 38-39 weeks, labor induction offer if EFW >=4000g)
outcome: Diagnostic yield of third-trimester scan for neonatal macrosomia prediction
cohort: Women who delivered at a tertiary center between July 2021 and July 2022, specifically comparing those with macrosomic newborns (>=4000 g) who had prenatal suspicion of macrosomia versus those who did not.
finding: The third-trimester ultrasound scan had low detection rates for neonatal macrosomia, and active management based on prenatal suspicion did not improve perinatal outcomes (including mode of delivery, shoulder dystocia, or perineal tear rates) compared to unsuspected neonatal macrosomia.
mod_finding: No significant differences were found in mode of delivery, shoulder dystocia, or perineal tear rates when comparing prenatally suspected macrosomic newborns who underwent active management versus unsuspected macrosomic newborns.
birth_weight: Neonates >=4000 g; average 3975g (+-285g) in the actively managed group.
